name: PARRY-style mood (ours, after Colby 1972)
source: elizita tier 5: our own script, modelled on Kenneth Colby's published description of PARRY (Stanford, 1972). Mood uses the same in-browser sentence model as tier 4 (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, Apache-2.0).
about: In 1972 the psychiatrist Kenneth Colby built PARRY, a simulation of a man with paranoid schizophrenia. Where ELIZA reflected you back, PARRY had an inner life: three numbers for fear, anger and mistrust that rose and fell with what you said. In a famous test, psychiatrists reading transcripts could tell PARRY from real patients only about as often as chance would predict.

This is our own version of that idea, running on the same engine. The persona is like Colby's: Frank, 28, a post office clerk in hospital, who goes to the races, fell out with a bookie and thinks the Mafia is after him. Talking about horses leads to bookies, and bookies lead to the Mafia.

Each message is compared, by meaning, with example phrases that raise or lower each mood ("you are crazy" raises anger; "I believe you" lowers it). The closest match moves the level, and every level drifts back toward calm by one point a turn. You can watch the meters in the workings under each reply, and here.

The rules read those levels: the same question gets a friendly, guarded, evasive or hostile answer depending on how he feels. Push anger or fear to 18 and he walks out, just as Colby's PARRY could end an interview.
Like tier 4, when no pattern fits exactly, the model finds the closest of his patterns by meaning. It never writes words; it only chooses.
